amendments.method: surgical — one hash replaced in place; `auditfences --baseline` NOT run
amendments.reason: The baseline is keyed by whole-file sha256, so ANY edit to a legacy file un-exempts every pre-existing un-fenced declaration in it, not just the edited lines. `companies` (the table declaration at line 13) predates spec 026 and was exempt at capture on 2026-07-01. It fell out of the baseline on an earlier commit and stayed out through SPEC-132/T002, which added four correctly-fenced lifecycle columns inside the table literal. Re-hashing restores that one pre-existing exemption and grants no new one: the only top-level declaration in the file is `companies` itself, and everything SPEC-132 added is inside a [SCOPE 132 / T002] fence.
restores: UNFENCED_DECL src/db/schema/company.ts:13 — un-fenced top-level declaration: table companies
amendments.notRunAndWhy: `auditfences --baseline` rewrites the payload from a fresh tree scan. It would drop the `deferred` ledger entirely (it writes only capturedAt + files) and would silently exempt the un-fenced declarations in all 212 baselined files that have drifted since capture, plus any file added since.
